question: It's said that members of the Astrea family who accomplish great deeds with the sword are given the name “Van.” Does that mean all of the Sword Saints throughout history have had “Van” in their names? And how many people who weren't Sword Saints, like Wilhelm, have been given the name “Van”?
answer:
Basically, every “Sword Saint” throughout history who acquired the “Divine Protection of the Sword Saint” has had “Van” in their name. In the first place, inheriting the title of “Sword Saint” is itself something close to accomplishing a great deed.

Wilhelm, on the other hand, is an extremely rare case because he earned it in a position unrelated to the “Divine Protection of the Sword Saint.” There was also an intention to give him a certain amount of prestige so that he could marry into the Astrea family, but of course, that wouldn't have been possible if his abilities weren't worthy of it.

So I don't think there have been many people who were able to receive it. None of Theresia's brothers received it, either.

When it comes to deeds significant enough to earn the name, you'd have to win a major war or produce some other clearly substantial achievement before anyone would accept it. There would also be people around asking, “Is this guy really worthy of receiving a name on the same level as the ‘Sword Saint’?”

So, there aren't many people who have received it. Wilhelm-san is an exceptional case.
